I’m playing Metal Gear Solid for the first time and wow, it is a perfect example of games which are supposed to be all-time beloved classics but do not hold up on any level today. My list of complaints with this awful game is growing during every painful sequence, and I don’t know if I’ll even have the patience to finish it.

The graphics suck. Everyone looks like polygonal robots with no features.

The dialogue is retarded, all about stupid platitudes like love blooming on a battlefield and other dumb shit.

He shoots Sniper Wolf to within an inch of her life then lovingly tells her she’s an honorable wolf or some bullshit. Painfully cheesy.

Half the time your peripheral vision is blacked out, making the visuals even worse.

Speaking of visuals, the environment is bland, colorless, and uninteresting. The only change is when you’re outside in the snow which is also bland and featureless.

You have to use body armor like an item and it isn’t effective when it’s not equipped??? So stupid.

You have to equip a card key that’s supposed to work remotely anyway, just to get through a door??? Stupid.

Top-down view so you can’t even see ten feet in front of you.

Half the time your radar is jammed and worthless, yet still takes up about an eighth of your screen.

You can’t use the sniper rifle without taking fucking pills first.

The game doesn’t give you any health rations after a major boss battle (Liquid in the Hind) then expects you to immediately fight four invisible guys in an elevator.

Could be wrong but I’m pretty sure the game literally never tells you you can sneak up and choke people.

Snake, supposed black ops badass with rippling biceps, can only throw grenades about five feet like a sissy girl.

Despite touting itself as a stealth game (the subtitle is Tactical Espionage Action), there is hardly any stealth action whatsoever and what little there is, is made completely annoying by the fact that, again, half the time your radar is jammed and you can’t see ten feet in front of you. Mind you, I don’t even really like stealth games. However the first few minutes of the game, which are generally supposed to be your training/intro period, made it seem like you would be sneaking around and avoiding enemies’ cones of vision when really that doesn’t turn out to be the case.

Some of the fourth-wall breaking attempts of the game are retarded and show no foresight for future gamers. For example how the FUCK am I supposed to know Meryl’s codec frequency if I’m playing the game 22 years later and don’t have a manual in my used game case?

Also how the FUCK would anyone ever know to unplug the controller and plug it into the 2nd port during the Psycho Mantis battle?! That is just bullshit.

The game gives you a hundred inventory items some of which you never have any indication of what the fuck to do with, such as the cardboard boxes and handkerchief. I looked up in a guide that the handkerchief keeps wolves from attacking you, but this is not signaled well in the game. Other items/weapons you use once or twice then not again, and they just take up space and time to cycle through. For example the cigarettes have only one purpose which is to see laser traps (how the hell would you know this by the way?) but are rendered completely obsolete when you get thermal goggles.

At the end of the game Snake and Meryl are basically professing their love for each other and committing to live together, literally riding off into the sunset (sunrise), after having known each other for less than 18 hours... most of that time having been spent separated. This also includes more incredibly cheesy dialogue.

Every boss has a period of invincibility after you damage them, yet Snake does not, so they can endlessly damage you. For example in the 2nd fight with Vulcan Raven he can basically one-hit kill you because if you fall down you lie there like an idiot for like five seconds before getting up, and can be hit by his machine gun during all this until dead. I always hate when control is taken away from the player for that long.

The final boss fight is endless, and has like a ten minute cut scene awkwardly inserted right in the middle.

These are not even all the complaints I can think of about this game. I finished it, and I’m trying to find the positives. I guess the ending was okay, and finally showed some colorful scenery. The art style is I guess not that bad for the hardware, and the beginning of the game was super intense and led me to believe it would be awesome. The advanced technology and high-tech lingo people used in the game were pretty cool too.

But overall, I did not like Metal Gear Solid. Since I played it for the first time in 2020, I obviously don’t have nostalgia for it but I’m sure some people have fondness for it since they experienced it during its time.

I would be glad to hear people’s defense of the game, or what they liked about it. Maybe I’m being too hard on it... but that was not a very fun 13 hours for me.
